theme: wildcard: an Airbnb superhost / small property manager who uses open-s
ideas: 1. Event-demand APIs that dynamic-pricing tools (PriceLabs/Wheelhouse/Beyond) plug into to raise/lower nightly rates around concerts, festivals, school holidays, sports (PredictHQ) -> HIT, real official SDKs found.

2. Cleaning/turnover scheduling apps (Turno/TurnoverBnB, Breezeway, Properly) that hosts use between guest stays -> the API surface implies a per-property turnover-count = nights-booked proxy, but no public data, only paid-API wrappers -> partial hit (method only, needs own account).

3. Self-hosted / open-source PMS and channel-manager tools that sync Airbnb+Booking.com+Vrbo calendars for small hosts (RentTools.io, Beds24, Channex, Hospitable) -> HIT, several real repos, all method/API-wrapper not stored data.

4. Multi-listing 'financial exporter' scripts individual hosts wrote for their own PMS (export nights/ADR/revenue to CSV) -> HIT one concrete example (Hospitable financial exporter); shows exact schema a real host's system captures.

5. Smart-lock / keyless-entry API wrappers (RemoteLock, Igloohome, Nuki, Schlage) that hosts use for check-in codes -> could reveal check-in/checkout timestamps aggregated across a property manager's portfolio -> MISS, could not find a public-data repo (only official closed SDKs), not pursued further given time budget.

6. Noise-monitoring / occupancy-sensor device API wrappers (NoiseAware, Minut) that hosts use for party/overcapacity detection -> MISS, GitHub search for 'minut' is swamped by unrelated 'minute/minutes' repos; no signal found in the time available.

7. Short-term-rental insurance / damage-claim platforms (Proper Insurance, Rentalguard, CBIZ) whose claims volume could proxy booking volume/incident rate -> MISS, not searched (no public repos expected; paid B2B claims data, flagged for a follow-up agent).

8. Municipal/host-facing occupancy-tax (transient occupancy tax / TOT) calculators and rate-lookup tools bundled into host software or GST/tax billing modules of open-source PMS (e.g. Kamra-PMS) -> weak hit; a PMS repo advertises tax billing but the exact rate tables were not verified due to a WebFetch rate limit.

9. Cross-OTA 'protocol' efforts to make short-term-rental listings machine-readable/bookable across platforms (openstr-protocol) -> possible hit (seen on a GitHub topics page) but not independently verified with its own repo page; flag for follow-up.

10. High-frequency historical FX tick data repos (used by pricing tools and treasury desks, not travel-specific) as a finer-grained alternative to the FRED daily FX series already held -> HIT, one well-starred repo with committed multi-year 1-minute FX/commodity/index data.

candidates.name: predicthq/sdk-py
candidates.what_it_holds: Official MIT-licensed Python client (27 stars, 341 commits, updated 5 May 2026) for the PredictHQ Events/Demand-Intelligence API. Endpoints: Events (concerts, festivals, sports, conferences, public + school holidays, severe weather, term/academic dates, community events, disasters) globally, ranked by predicted attendance/impact; Places; Features (pre-aggregated demand-forecast features by location/date, e.g. a 'PHQ Rank' or attendance sum per day per area); Broadcasts (TV viewership tied to events); polygon/radius impact-area queries. This is the exact event-demand feed that vacation-rental dynamic-pricing engines (PriceLabs, Wheelhouse, Beyond Pricing all cite PredictHQ as a data partner) plug into to move nightly rates around demand shocks. No data files are committed; it is a live-API pull (free tier exists but usage-limited).
candidates.why_useful: Maps directly onto CONTEXT.md gap #11 (events/shocks: FIFA World Cup 2026, concerts, conferences) and #17 (event-study/nowcasting methods). A PredictHQ 'Features' pull by market (NA/EMEA/LatAm/APAC metros) around the 3Q26 World Cup window or major-market festival calendars could be turned into an independent, point-in-time event-density regressor for nights/ADR that is not derived from Airbnb data itself.
candidates.time_coverage: live/forward-looking event calendar (also has historical event coverage back several years via the API)
candidates.size_hint: code-only client library, no committed data

candidates.name: predicthq/phq-data-science-docs
candidates.what_it_holds: PredictHQ's own MIT-licensed data-science documentation/notebooks (17 stars, updated 27 Aug 2026) showing how to turn the raw Events API into demand-forecast features for verticals including accommodation.
candidates.why_useful: Companion methods doc to sdk-py; useful as a template for building an events-based demand feature set for ABNB nights/ADR nowcasting without re-deriving the feature engineering from scratch.

candidates.name: predicthq/streamlit-accommodation-demo
candidates.what_it_holds: Streamlit demo app (1 star) built by PredictHQ specifically for the 'accommodation' vertical, wiring PredictHQ Events/Location-Insights into a demand dashboard. No license file found, no data committed; it calls the live API and needs a PredictHQ key.
candidates.why_useful: Confirms PredictHQ explicitly markets an accommodation-demand use case (i.e. this is exactly what STR pricing tools ingest) and gives a runnable reference implementation for pulling an events-based demand index by market — useful scaffolding rather than a dataset.

candidates.name: predicthq/aws-sagemaker-demand-forecasting-example
candidates.what_it_holds: MIT-licensed worked example (also mirrored as an official aws-samples repo) forecasting demand with AWS SageMaker XGBoost using PredictHQ event features as exogenous regressors.
candidates.why_useful: A concrete, runnable nowcasting-with-mixed-frequency-events template (gap #17) that could be adapted to regress ABNB nights/ADR residuals on an event-density feature built from PredictHQ.
candidates.geography: global (example uses generic retail-style demand, adaptable)
candidates.size_hint: notebook + small sample data for the demo

candidates.name: NextLevelManagementAdvisors/turno-mcp
candidates.what_it_holds: AGPL-3.0 multi-tenant MCP server (updated 10 Sep 2026, 34 commits) wrapping the Turno (formerly TurnoverBnB) v2 REST API: 49 tools covering properties, bookings, blocked dates, cleaning assignments/projects, cleaners, checklists, problems, reviews, webhooks. Requires the operator's own Turno API credentials — no public data included.
candidates.why_useful: Turno is the dominant STR cleaning-scheduler; its 'bookings'/'blocked dates' objects are effectively a real-time occupancy calendar per managed property. Documents exactly what fields a professional property manager's turnover system tracks (checkout->clean->next-checkin cadence), which is the ground-truth structure any nights/turnover proxy would need to reconstruct if a cooperating host/PM ever shared exports.
candidates.size_hint: code only, no data (paid API key required, per-account access only)

candidates.name: Gribadan/RentTools.io
candidates.what_it_holds: MIT-licensed, self-hosted open-source PMS for small STR hosts (23 stars, updated 13 Sep 2026): syncs Airbnb + Booking.com calendars via iCal, automates cleaning schedules, extracts guest passport data. Live product at renttools.io. No comp/market data committed — it is host-side software over each user's own calendars.
candidates.why_useful: Shows the exact iCal-export mechanics (Airbnb and Booking.com both expose per-listing .ics export URLs) that any small-scale, ToS-compliant occupancy-proxy build would use; also a candidate 'better mousetrap' if the project ever wanted to invite cooperating hosts to contribute their own calendar exports for a bottom-up occupancy panel.

candidates.name: keithah/hospitable-python
candidates.what_it_holds: MIT-licensed Python SDK (2 stars, updated 3 Nov 2025) for the Hospitable Public API v2. Covers vacation-rental properties, reservations, calendar, messaging, and reviews. Hospitable is a mid-size multi-channel PMS managing thousands of Airbnb/Vrbo/Booking.com listings; the API exposes per-reservation nightly rate, length of stay, channel, and property/market metadata to the account owner.
candidates.why_useful: Documents the field-level schema (ADR-equivalent nightly rate, LOS, channel/source, market) a professional multi-listing operator's system captures per booking — the same fields needed to build a bottom-up nights/ADR panel, if a cooperating Hospitable-using PM ever exported their own portfolio.
candidates.geography: wherever the connected account's listings are
candidates.size_hint: code only, no data (requires the operator's own API key)

candidates.name: timwoodland/hospitable_financial_exporter
candidates.what_it_holds: Small unlicensed Python script (updated 15 Jun 2026) written by an actual Hospitable-using host/PM to export their own financial data (per-listing revenue/booking detail) from Hospitable to CSV for a chosen date range.
candidates.why_useful: A real, in-the-wild example of a small property manager exporting exactly the revenue/occupancy fields (by listing, by date range) this project would want in bulk; useful chiefly as a schema reference / proof that hosts routinely build these exports themselves, not as a source of usable third-party data (single-account, no data committed).

candidates.name: webrenew/channex-mcp
candidates.what_it_holds: MIT-licensed MCP server (5 stars, updated 18 Jun 2026) for Channex.io's channel-manager API: create/read/update/delete properties, room_types, and rate_plans, which Channex then distributes to Airbnb, Booking.com, Expedia and other OTAs simultaneously.
candidates.why_useful: Channex sits between many small PMs and every major OTA at once; its rate-plan/ARI (availability-rate-inventory) objects are the same data a host pushes to Airbnb, so the schema shows what a cross-OTA comp/rate panel would need to look like. Requires the operator's own Channex credentials; no public data.
candidates.geography: wherever the connected account's properties are

candidates.name: minical/channex-integration
candidates.what_it_holds: MIT-licensed extension (7 stars, updated 25 May 2026) integrating the miniCal PMS with Channex to connect to OTAs including Booking.com, Airbnb, and Expedia.
candidates.why_useful: A second, independent confirmation of the Channex cross-OTA ARI schema (see channex-mcp above); low incremental value beyond that.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: same underlying Channex cross-OTA schema as webrenew/channex-mcp

candidates.name: philipperemy/FX-1-Minute-Data
candidates.what_it_holds: Apache-2.0 repo (683 stars, updated 10 Sep 2026) titled HISTDATA: a simple downloader/API plus multi-year committed sample data for 1-minute (and tick-level) historical FX pairs, crude oil, and stock indices, sourced from HistData.com.
candidates.why_useful: We currently hold only FX 'schedules' per CONTEXT.md; this is a finer-grained (1-minute), multi-year, easy one-command-pull historical FX series that could sharpen intra-quarter FX-mix timing for the ADR ex-FX/FX split, more granular than daily FRED FX series already held.
candidates.time_coverage: multi-year historical, 1-minute bars, up to date per README
candidates.size_hint: downloader + example data; full history pulled via included tool (potentially large)
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: extends the FX schedules already held to intraday/1-minute granularity

candidates.name: ArpitKanungo/mock-pricelabs-api
candidates.what_it_holds: A mock/toy implementation of the PriceLabs API (0 stars, updated 2 May 2026), no real market data — a testing stub only.
candidates.why_useful: Confirms PriceLabs (a dominant STR dynamic-pricing tool many hosts use) has a documented API shape worth knowing about, but this particular repo has nothing usable; flagged only so a follow-up agent doesn't re-discover and re-evaluate it.

notes: Ten wildcard ideas (superhost/small-PM tooling angle), hit/miss noted inline in the 'ideas' list above. Session-wide WebSearch budget was already exhausted (200/200) before this scout could run a single query, so this run leaned entirely on `gh search repos` (used well past the nominal 5-call budget because many single-idea queries returned 0 hits and had to be reformulated) plus WebFetch against github.com/topics/* pages (which were NOT rate-limited) once github.com/search?... via WebFetch started 429'ing (Retry-After 3600s). Recommend a follow-up agent with a fresh WebSearch budget try: (a) 'openstr-protocol' and 'guesty-mcp-server' directly (seen on a topics page, URLs not independently confirmed here), (b) Kamra-PMS (open-source hotel/STR PMS advertising 'GST/tax billing' — could contain an actual occupancy-tax rate table, unverified), (c) StayOps, Roost, LibreProperty, Burrow/ReserveLogic (seen listed under github.com/topics/vacation-rental but not individually verified), (d) NoiseAware/Minut/RemoteLock/Igloohome API wrappers (searched but swamped by irrelevant results under generic terms; try exact vendor-name + 'api-client' or check each vendor's own developer-docs page for a linked open-source SDK), (e) STR insurance/damage-claim platforms (Proper Insurance, Rentalguard) — not searched at all, pure idea. Also worth a second pass: 'short-term-rentals-warehouse' (a repo name surfaced on the short-term-rental topics page describing 'pipeline and visualization tools examining Airbnb's impact on urban housing markets' — could be a duplicate or an improvement on our existing Inside Airbnb holdings; WebFetch to confirm its URL/contents 429'd every time it was attempted). None of the STR-specific PMS/channel-manager/cleaning-scheduler repos found here carry usable public data — they are uniformly single-account API wrappers requiring the operator's own paid-vendor credentials, so their value is entirely as schema/method references (what fields a real host or PM's software actually tracks), not as pullable datasets. The one genuinely new pullable-data idea from this run is PredictHQ (predicthq/sdk-py): it is the literal event-demand feed that STR dynamic-pricing tools (PriceLabs, Wheelhouse, Beyond) build their pricing recommendations on, directly relevant to the World Cup 2026 / events-and-shocks gap (#11), and distinct from anything already catalogued.
